environment.name: development
environment.authentication: Normal BetterAuth HTTP sign-in, same supplied session cookie across variants; no bypass.

method.p95: Nearest rank: sorted[ceil(0.95 * n) - 1]; 20 samples use the 19th sorted value, 3 samples use the maximum.
method.duration: Monotonic elapsed from fetch start through full body consumption; redirects are not followed.
method.validation: HTTP200 plus valid API data envelope; HTML streamed redirect/error fallbacks are failures. No response bodies, cookies, credentials, actors, SQL or SQL parameters are retained here.
method.coldOutput: .next from a fresh stopped snapshot compiler output; owned caches pruned after archival.
method.resourceSampling: Sum of launcher descendant RSS and ps percentCPU sampled every500ms; old-space budget is per Node process, not aggregate RSS.
method.apiTiming: Driver-dispatch count includes auth, transaction and session-control statements. SQL duration sums driver elapsed; pool waits are separately recorded. Concurrent sums may exceed request wall time.
method.hmr: Temporary health-response header edit, then exact source restore. Webpack4 used an immediate restore check and its stale result is invalid for restoration latency. Final webpack8 polls until the header disappears with HTTP200 within90s. Turbopack edit probes timed out in the frozen app.
method.sameDataComparison: Source hash and allowlisted paged=1/dashboard selections match across four selected variants. API response sizes match, but the live database and background activity were not isolated; byte equality does not establish data identity.
method.comparisonStatus: Four aligned variants completed across three launchers. The supplemental unpaged webpack8 run and all earlier invalid or incomplete attempts are retained separately.
method.queryRecording: Earlier helper rows stripped query strings; allowlisted paged and view selectors have been recovered where all matching GET log lines agree. The updated helper records those allowlisted selectors directly; other values and identifiers are omitted.

caveats: Cold routes are visited sequentially Work,People,PMSsettings,readAPIs,health; later routes can reuse shared modules compiled by Work. This is first-hit route cold timing, not an isolated new process per individual route.
HTTP full-document requests are not browser client navigation or Core Web Vitals; the public1.5s navigation target needs separate authenticated browser verification.
The snapshot source/hash is fixed; the shared development database, normal jobs, browser traffic, other CPU workloads and operating-system file caches are not isolated.
Snapshot copying and earlier rounds warm operating-system caches. Installed dependency contents are assumed stable, with lockfile and contained dependency tree reused.

The supplemental unpaged webpack8 cold1/cold2 logs had 66/50 GETs versus 7 selected requests; compilation and RSS were confounded by extra People, Front POS/PMS, navigation and login activity. Corrected webpack8 cold1/cold2 had 10/7 GETs; cold3 had 323 including 280 warm requests and HMR/background requests.
The Turbo4 continuation ran later after recovered development jobs were running; observed warm differences from Turbo8 do not establish heap causality.

Turbopack frozen-app HMR failed at both budgets. Root also observed original workspace Turbo API route edits fail to reflect within 45 seconds while a component Fast Refresh check passed. Installed code intends route-handler subscriptions without a browser; the watcher/server HMR cause remains unresolved.

All four aligned variants request Work summary?paged=1 and return 25,555 bytes. People returns 318,889 and PMS dashboard 3,066 bytes consistently. Supplemental unpaged webpack8 returns 518,362 bytes because its Work selector differs; no live data growth is established. HTML/bundler variation and byte equality do not establish business behavior or data identity.
Invalid custom-output, source-change, disk-failure and externally interrupted experiments are retained separately. Missing disk-failure durations/statuses cannot be reconstructed.
Final restoration uses current original workspace source, which can differ from frozen benchmark source.

The earliest source-change launcher predates body-validation fields: it records5 unvalidated HTTP200 responses,1 Work timeout and1 health503. Those HTTP200 results are not retroactively treated as validated successes or failures.

Work driver timing retains typical24 dispatches and occasional385-dispatch outliers with large summed SQL/pool durations. These are consistent with Work snapshot rebuild work and are not attributed solely to compiler/heap choice.
Supplemental webpack8 completed before its Work query selection error was found and remains outside the aligned comparison. Corrected webpack8 explicitly preserves paged=1 and view=dashboard.

Corrected webpack8 public Work warm p95 is 2524.535ms with median 257.960ms; retain this outlier. Local HTTP document medians are below the provisional 1 second response target. Public HTTP document medians below 1.5 seconds do not establish the client navigation target; separate browser verification is required, and not every public request is under 1.5 seconds.

Subsequent finite normal-session bursts observed a Next automatic used-heap threshold restart under the aged webpack/4 GiB worker. The final development fallback is provisionally 8 GiB for headroom; the fresh 8 GiB finite run was not a controlled long-session or causal heap comparison. See browser-concurrency evidence for every request, process transition and failure.

chosenDevelopmentDefault.reason: The aged 4 GiB development worker reached Next’s automatic used-heap restart threshold during the finite burst. The explicit fresh 8 GiB run and subsequent component HMR completed with the listener unchanged and no automatic memory restart log events. The selected budget provides headroom; it is not an established latency improvement or sustained heap-retention solution.
chosenDevelopmentDefault.overridePolicy: Explicit 4 GiB/8 GiB selection and caller NODE_OPTIONS remain supported.
remainingLimitations: Finite GET bursts and a single component edit/restore do not establish long-session reliability.
Heap retention and sustained memory behavior still require investigation.
No claim that webpack/8 GiB is the fastest variant.
chosenDevelopmentDefault.decisionSequence: The matrix initially favored webpack/4 GiB for correct route hot reload. Later normal-session evidence showed the automatic heap-threshold restart at 4 GiB, so the final operational default was raised to 8 GiB without claiming faster request latency.
